passages.original: οἱ δὲ λέγουσιν μύθους ἡμῖν, οἱ δʼ Αἰσώπου τι γέλοιον·
passages.english: Some of them tell us fables, and others something funny of Aesop's.
passages.notes: Part of a list of ways defendants try to win over the jurors (Wasps, c. line 566); the passage begins mid-sequence.

passages.original: ὥσπερ Ἑκάταιον, πανταχοῦ πρὸ τῶν θυρῶν.
passages.english: like a Hecataeum, everywhere in front of the doors.
passages.notes: A Hecataeum (Hekataion) was a small shrine or image of Hecate set up before house doors. The line is given without context; in the play it describes something found everywhere before doors, possibly the shrine of Lycus mentioned nearby.
